Someone more inclined may want to rewrite this as I am really not the wiki-editor type. What I am, is a person who pays attention to the way language is used. There is some very miniscule discussion of Robert Jordan's use of language here, truly, something that should really be considered insulting to such a great writer. Some discussion is given to character names and their connections to names of characters from other myths, however very little is given to Jordan's other language plays. This is perhaps nowhere greater than the Aelfinn/Ellfinn connection to Elven. To the tall, fair-haired-and-eyed Aiel, also a play on Elven, or Germanic Alwin;  and the raken and to'raken to drake, or rake, or draken / dragon. To'raken is a spelling alteration, but doesn't it sound a bit like draken??? To'raken, draken, t'raken, draken, traken, draken, ????  Which is a variation of drake or dragon??? Someone who maintains this wiki should spend a little more time talking about the other NUMEROUS ways language is used like this in Jordan's work. (Added by [[User:Coyotefishsmile]])
